[[Todd Muller]]
[[Judith Collins]] | deputy2 = [[Matt Doocey]] | predecessor2 = [[Jami-Lee Ross]] | successor2 = [[Matt Doocey]] | profession = Farmer | spouse = Louis Kuriger | party = [[New Zealand National Party|National]] | children = | website = | footnotes = }} '''Barbara Joan Kuriger''' (born 1961){{cite web |url= https://www.parliament.nz/media/6305/roll-of-members-of-the-new-zealand-house-of-representatives-1854-onwards.pdf |title=Roll of members of the New Zealand House of Representatives, 1854 onwards |date=24 May 2019 |publisher=[[New Zealand Parliament]] |access-date=3 September 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200903095934/https://www.parliament.nz/media/6305/roll-of-members-of-the-new-zealand-house-of-representatives-1854-onwards.pdf|archive-date=3 September 2020|url-status=live}} is a New Zealand politician who has served as [[Deputy Speaker of the New Zealand House of Representatives]] since December 2023. A member of the [[New Zealand National Party|National Party]], Kuriger was first elected as the Member of Parliament (MP) for [[Taranaki-King Country]] in 2014. == Early life == Kuriger was born in [[Ōpunake]] and was raised on a dairy farm. She married Louis Kuriger, a dairy farmer. They have three children.{{Cite web |date=21 October 2014 |title=Kuriger, Barbara - Address in Reply |url=https://www.parliament.nz/en/pb/hansard-debates/rhr/document/51HansS_20141021_00000373/kuriger-barbara-address-in-reply |access-date=18 December 2024 |website=New Zealand Parliament}}{{Cite web |date=21 September 2016 |title=Kuriger, Barbara - Taranaki Iwi Claims Settlement Bill — Second Reading |url=https://www.parliament.nz/en/pb/hansard-debates/rhr/document/HansS_20160921_127800000/kuriger-barbara |access-date=18 December 2024 |website=New Zealand Parliament}} ==Farming career== Kuriger is a farmer, shareholder and director of three family-owned farming businesses. With her husband Louis, she won the Taranaki Sharemilker of the Year title in 1978.{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=15 April 2013 |title=First family to claim second generation of awards success |url=https://www.ruralnewsgroup.co.nz/dairy-news/dairy-management/first-family-to-claim-second-generation-of-awards-success |access-date=2024-12-17 |website=Rural News Group |language=en-gb}} Kuriger has served on the boards of several companies and institutions including DairyNZ, Dairy Training Limited, Primary ITO, New Zealand Young Farmers, Taratahi Agricultural Training Centre, Te Kauta, Venture Taranaki Trust, the Dairy Women's Network, and the New Zealand Rural Games Trust.{{cite news |date=17 June 2014 |title=Rural Games to get off the ground in Queenstown |url=http://www.scene.co.nz/rural-games-to-get-off-the-ground-in-queenstown/317526a1.page |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303214617/http://www.scene.co.nz/rural-games-to-get-off-the-ground-in-queenstown/317526a1.page |archive-date=3 March 2016 |access-date=2 November 2020 |work=Mountain Scene |publisher=[[Allied Press]]}} In 2012, she won the title of Dairy Woman of the Year.{{cite news |title=Kuriger National's pick |url=http://www.stuff.co.nz/taranaki-daily-news/news/9912327/Kuriger-Nationals-pick |access-date=2 November 2020 |work=[[Taranaki Daily News]] |publisher=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |date=7 April 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201102085140/http://www.stuff.co.nz/taranaki-daily-news/news/9912327/Kuriger-Nationals-pick |archive-date=2 November 2020}} Kuriger was criticised for her role as a member of the Taratahi Agricultural Training Centre board in 2015 when it was under investigation by the Serious Fraud Office. Kuriger had been a board member from 2012 to 2014 but denied knowledge of any misdoing; Labour MP [[David Cunliffe]] said Kuriger could not claim to be ignorant of what had occurred.{{cite news |last=Lee |first=Hannah |date=16 September 2015 |title=Kuriger must have known about Taratahi 'rorts' – Cunliffe |url=http://www.stuff.co.nz/taranaki-daily-news/news/72120447/kuriger-must-have-known-about-taratahi-rorts--cunliffe |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170808200455/http://www.stuff.co.nz/taranaki-daily-news/news/72120447/kuriger-must-have-known-about-taratahi-rorts--cunliffe |archive-date=8 August 2017 |access-date=25 April 2017 |work=[[Taranaki Daily News]] |publisher=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]]}} Kuriger is a former director of Oxbow Dairies Ltd which was charged with multiple counts of animal cruelty and neglect. Kuriger ceased being a director in 2014, while her husband Louis was still a director until late 2018 during which period the bulk of the charges were laid and offences committed. Their son, Tony, who was also a director of the company, pleaded guilty in January 2020 for causing "prolonged and severe pain" to the animals in his care.{{cite news|url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/crime/119076696/treatment-plan-for-lame-cows-may-have-made-condition-worse-court-hears|title=Politician's son pleads guilty to ill-treating dairy cows; charges against husband dropped |work=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]]|date=28 January 2020|first=Sam|last=Kilmister|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200321140204/https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/crime/119076696/treatment-plan-for-lame-cows-may-have-made-condition-worse-court-hears|archive-date=21 March 2020|url-status=live}} ==Political career== {{NZ parlbox header|align=left}} {{NZ parlbox |term=51st |start={{NZ election link year|2014}} |end=2017 |list=58 |party=New Zealand National Party |electorate=[[Taranaki-King Country]] }} {{NZ parlbox |term=52nd |start={{NZ election link year|2017}} |end=2020 |list=28 |party=New Zealand National Party |electorate=Taranaki-King Country }} {{NZ parlbox |term=53rd |start={{NZ election link year|2020}} |end=2023 |list=20 |party=New Zealand National Party |electorate=Taranaki-King Country }} {{NZ parlbox |term=54th |start={{NZ election link year|2023}} |end=present |list=36 |party=New Zealand National Party |electorate=Taranaki-King Country }} {{End}}In April 2014, Kuriger was selected as National's candidate in [[Taranaki-King Country]] to replace the retiring [[Shane Ardern]]. During the [[2014 New Zealand general election]], she won Taranaki-King Country for National by a margin of 16,773 votes.{{cite web |title=Official Count Results – Taranaki-King Country |url=https://archive.electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2014/electorate-50.html |publisher=[[Electoral Commission (New Zealand)|Electoral Commission]] |access-date=2 November 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200122162316/http://archive.electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2014/electorate-50.html |archive-date=22 January 2020 |date=10 October 2014 |url-status=live}} Her maiden statement, given on 21 October 2014, was the second to be given in the [[51st New Zealand Parliament|51st Parliament]]'s [[Address in Reply|address in reply debate]]. In her first term, Kuriger served as deputy chair of the health committee and as a member of the primary production committee, and was a junior National Party [[Whip (politics)|whip]].{{cite web |title=Kuriger, Barbara - New Zealand Parliament |url=https://www.parliament.nz/en/mps-and-electorates/members-of-parliament/kuriger-barbara/ |access-date=18 December 2024 |page=}} Reelected at the [[2017 New Zealand general election]],{{cite web |title=Taranaki-King Country – Official Result |url=http://archive.electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2017/electorate-details-50.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200117212855/http://archive.electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2017/electorate-details-50.html |archive-date=17 January 2020 |access-date=2 November 2020 |publisher=[[Electoral Commission (New Zealand)|Electoral Commission]]}} she served as the National Party's [[Senior Whip of the National Party|senior whip]] from 2018 to 2020.{{cite news |last1=McCulloch |first1=Craig |last2=Scotcher |first2=Katie |title=Shane Reti becomes new deputy leader of the National Party |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/430255/shane-reti-becomes-new-deputy-leader-of-the-national-party |access-date=10 November 2020 |publisher=[[RNZ]] |date=10 November 2020}} In March 2018 a member's bill in her name seeking to impose penalties on the parents of children before the [[Youth Court of New Zealand|youth court]] was debated and lost.{{Cite web |date=2018-02-22 |title=Four members' bills drawn from ballot |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/351035/four-members-bills-drawn-from-ballot |access-date=2024-12-18 |website=RNZ |language=en-nz}}{{Cite web |date=21 March 2018 |title=Oranga Tamariki (Parent's and Guardian's Responsibility) Amendment Bill — First Reading |url=https://www.parliament.nz/en/pb/hansard-debates/rhr/combined/HansDeb_20180321_20180321_32/ |website=New Zealand Parliament}} Briefly in 2020 she also the party's spokesperson for food safety, rural communities, and women, and chaired Parliament's primary production committee. After the [[2020 New Zealand general election]], in which she won a third term,{{cite web |title=Taranaki-King Country – Official Result |url=https://www.electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2020/electorate-details-50.html |access-date=13 November 2020 |publisher=[[Electoral Commission (New Zealand)|Electoral Commission]]}} she was appointed spokesperson for agriculture, energy and resources, and food safety.{{cite web |date=11 November 2020 |title=National Party leader Judith Collins reveals caucus reshuffle |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/430347/national-party-leader-judith-collins-reveals-caucus-reshuffle |access-date=18 December 2024 |website=RNZ}} She chaired the governance and administration committee from 2020 to 2021. When [[Christopher Luxon]] became the party leader in 2021, he appointed her as spokesperson for agriculture, biosecurity and food safety.{{cite news |last=Small |first=Zane |date=6 December 2021 |title=Judith Collins plunges to #19 in Christopher Luxon's reshuffle as Shane Reti, Chris Bishop keep top roles |url=https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/politics/2021/12/judith-collins-plunges-to-19-in-christopher-luxon-s-reshuffle-as-shane-reti-chris-bishop-keep-top-roles.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211206003626/https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/politics/2021/12/judith-collins-plunges-to-19-in-christopher-luxon-s-reshuffle-as-shane-reti-chris-bishop-keep-top-roles.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=6 December 2021 |work=[[Newshub]]}} In October 2022 Kuriger resigned from her agriculture, biosecurity, and food safety portfolios due to mismanaging conflicts of interest with the [[Ministry for Primary Industries (New Zealand)|Ministry for Primary Industries]] (MPI) over the prosecution of her husband and son.{{cite web |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/130174859/national-mp-barbara-kuriger-drops-agriculture-portfolios-over-blurred-line-in-family-dispute |title=National MP Barbara Kuriger drops agriculture portfolios over 'blurred line' in family dispute |publisher=Stuff |date=14 October 2022 |access-date=14 October 2022}} In December 2022, hundreds of pages of emails between Kuriger and MPI, obtained by [[Newsroom (website)|Newsroom]] under the [[Official Information Act 1982|Official Information Act]], revealed a pattern of personal attacks on MPI officials in relation to animal mistreatment charges filed against her son Tony. MPI commissioned Mike Heron KC to review its conduct in the case. That review cleared the ministry of any wrongdoing and found the investigation into Tony Kuriger was not motivated by political purposes, despite the Kurigers' repeated private and public claims to the contrary.{{Cite web |last=Daalder |first=Marc |date=17 December 2022 |title=MP's emails show pattern of personal attacks on ministry |url=https://www.newsroom.co.nz/mps-emails-show-pattern-of-personal-attacks-on-ministry |access-date=17 December 2022 |website=Newsroom}} Kuriger refused to resign from Parliament over the incident.{{Cite web |date=2023-01-19 |title=Kuriger says no plans to step down after family scandal aired |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/482723/kuriger-says-no-plans-to-step-down-after-family-scandal-aired |access-date=2024-12-18 |website=RNZ |language=en-nz}} Following a January 2023 shadow cabinet reshuffle, Kuriger was allocated the conservation portfolio but was moved outside of the shadow cabinet with no ranking.{{Cite news |title=National reshuffle: Luxon promotes former leaders Judith Collins, Todd Muller |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/politics/chris-bishop-judith-collins-and-todd-muller-winners-in-national-reshuffle/GSJOIE4DVNDA5CSUFBUZI6RK6U/ |date=19 January 2023 |access-date=19 January 2023 |work=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |language=en-NZ|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230119081812/https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/politics/chris-bishop-judith-collins-and-todd-muller-winners-in-national-reshuffle/GSJOIE4DVNDA5CSUFBUZI6RK6U/|archive-date=19 January 2023|url-status=live}} National returned to government for the first time in six years at the [[2023 New Zealand general election]]. Kuriger retained her electorate by a margin of 14,355 votes, defeating [[New Zealand Labour Party|Labour]] candidate [[Angela Roberts (politician)|Angela Roberts]],{{cite web |title=Taranaki-King Country – Official Result |url=https://www.electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2023/electorate-details-50.html |publisher=[[Electoral Commission (New Zealand)|Electoral Commission]] |access-date=16 December 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231210215713/https://www.electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2023/electorate-details-50.html |archive-date=10 December 2023 |date=3 November 2023 |url-status=live}} and was appointed [[Deputy Speaker of the New Zealand House of Representatives|Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives]].{{cite web |title=Appointments — Deputy Speaker and Assistant Speakers - New Zealand Parliament |url=https://www.parliament.nz/en/pb/hansard-debates/rhr/combined/HansDeb_20231206_20231206_36 |access-date=18 December 2024 |page=}} ==References== {{Reflist}} == External links == *[https://web.archive.org/web/20150529003252/https://www.national.org.nz/team/electorates/detail/central-north-island-region/taranaki---king-country National Party page for Taranaki-King Country] *[http://barbarakuriger.co.nz/ Barbara Kuriger's website] *[http://www.parliament.nz/en-nz/mpp/mps/current/51MP3511/kuriger-barbara Parliament website page for Barbara Kruiger] {{s-start}} {{s-par|nz}} {{s-bef|before=[[Shane Ardern]]}} {{s-ttl|title=[[Taranaki-King Country|Member of Parliament for Taranaki-King Country]]| years=2014–present}} {{s-inc}} {{s-end}} {{NZ National Party}} {{Current members of the New Zealand House of Representatives}} {{subject bar|auto=y|d=y|Politics|New Zealand}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Kuriger, Barbara}} [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:New Zealand National Party MPs]] [[Category:Members of the New Zealand House of Representatives]] [[Category:Women members of the New Zealand House of Representatives]] [[Category:New Zealand MPs for North Island electorates]] [[Category:21st-century New Zealand women politicians]] [[Category:Candidates in the 2014 New Zealand general election]] [[Category:Candidates in the 2017 New Zealand general election]] [[Category:Candidates in the 2020 New Zealand general election]] [[Category:Candidates in the 2023 New Zealand general election]] [[Category:1961 births]] [[Category:People from Ōpunake]]
